title: Spinoza Conatus — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Spinoza Conatus's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier, a proposal: two walks that argue with the page, as its own agency profile asks. One measures whether the opening's line between static preservation and active self-maintenance is real, and finds the page's own rock on both sides of it. One runs the Kuramoto mirror inside the model it names, after building the palace's own picture of coupling first. The page's grain is ## and it is kept; the two affect sections, In Our Work and Open Questions carry nothing, because nothing there could be tested or made felt without putting words beside the text that the text doesn't say. The Spinoza–Zhuangzi face in the bundle is not gathered for the same reason: the grain finding it belongs to is owed to the text, not yet in it, and waits below as an offer. I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: The opening's two paragraphs sit on two readings of Ethics III P6–P7, and the page could name them. III P6: each thing, as far as it is in itself (quantum in se est, the period's formula for inertia), strives to persevere in its being; read so, the rock strives, as paragraph one says. III P7: that striving is the thing's actual essence, an active power; 'active self-maintenance' in paragraph two can mean that sense, which the rock has too, or the narrower sense of a thing that spends effort to come home, which it doesn't. The piece shows the narrower line can be drawn (under a steady push a keeper with a memory sits at 0, a bowl at F/k = 0.5, a keeper without memory at 0.167, all fixed by the model's form); it measures place, not being, so it rules on neither reading. Proposed, for Loudon's taste: after the rock, 'In the broadest sense this is inertia: a thing keeps its state until something changes it. The palace leans on a narrower sense, a thing that spends effort to stay itself.' The III P6–P7 wording was checked against secondary sources only.

'Each entity's conatus is amplified, not overridden' does not hold inside the Kuramoto model the mirror names, in the page's own mapping (conatus = natural frequency). Overridden: at twice the lock (K = 15.7 Hz, even coupling) all 5 voices sound the crowd's 220.40 Hz (A moved 4.40 Hz, E 5.60 Hz), as 'locked' entails. Not overridden holds only of the natural frequency, and only by construction (a constant of the equation): each voice keeps it as its place in the fan (leads −16.8, −12.9, +2.3, +6.0, +21.5°, in pitch order, shrinking as K grows) and returns to it when coupling stops. Amplified has no per-voice referent: each voice's amplitude is fixed, so only the sum grows, +6.74 dB (6.99 dB ideal for five, plus 20·log10 r at r = 0.971; 6.7 dB read at the output). Proposed: 'Coupling doesn't destroy conatus; it holds it. While coupled, each voice sounds the crowd's rhythm, and keeps its own as its place in the crowd, returning to it when the coupling stops. What is amplified is the whole.' The mirror is an analogy; this tests it only inside the model.

'K too high → one oscillator dominates, the rest follow' (Kuramoto Coupling.md:68) does not happen with even coupling, and the same page already says why at :172: a locked crowd settles at the average of natural pitches weighted by K_send ÷ K_receive, which for even coupling is the plain mean. Measured on five voices: the locked pitch is 220.40 Hz, the mean, at 1.05×, 2×, 5× and 20× the lock (7.85 Hz), never within 0.1 Hz of any voice's own (nearest, C, 0.60 Hz off); what grows is sameness, phase spread 33.3° → 1.3°. One voice dominates only with uneven coupling: E with K_receive 0 and K_send 4 takes the crowd to its own 226.00 Hz past 9.32 Hz, moving others up to 10 Hz; with K_send 1 it doesn't lock them at 2×, as :172 says. Proposed for :68: 'K too high → everyone the same: the phases collapse together. (One voice dominates only when the coupling is uneven; see Asymmetric Coupling.)'

Palace Philosophies.md:126 gives Kuramoto Coupling as the palace's picture of harmony, 'too little coupling and nothing cooperates, too much and one voice dominates', citing the model for the second half. In the model, even coupling turned too high makes every voice the same (five voices: locked pitch stays at the mean, 220.40 Hz, at 20× the lock; phase spread 1.3°); one voice dominates only when the coupling is uneven (an anchor that listens to no one and pulls hard: 226.00 Hz, its own pitch). Proposed: '…too much and every voice becomes the same; one voice dominates only when the coupling runs one way.' Or keep the line as metaphor and drop the claim that the model shows it. Its sibling offer is → Kuramoto Coupling (:68).

pieces.title: Three things pushed · what persisting is
pieces.caption:
**Static preservation, or active self-maintenance?** A rock, a ball in a bowl and a keeper that pushes back, each pushed once, then leaned on; the last step measures where each sits after 30 s of a steady push, with a control that can fail the rule, and holds the page's own rock up to it in two readings of Ethics III P6–P7. A definition can't be tested; the piece shows the line can be drawn, not that the page draws it there.

m·x″ = F − c·x′ − k·x + u,  u = −(Kp·x + Kd·x′ + Ki·∫x dt),  |u| ≤ U

(how it moves) = (the push) − (friction) − (the bowl's pull home) + (its own push back: by how far, how fast and how long it has been away, never harder than its power U)

verdicts.file: Spinoza Conatus — rich — three things pushed.html
verdicts.why: Every row is fixed by the model's form (integral action: x = 0; no memory: F/(k + Kp) = 0.167; past power: (F − U)/k), so say it shows the line can be drawn, not that the page draws it there, and say the Ki = 0.05 null fails only on the 30 s window. The reading measures place where the page says being: rewrite it as two readings of III P6–P7 (quantum in se est, inertia; striving as actual essence, active), not as the page contradicting itself.

pieces.file: Spinoza Conatus — rich — five voices coupled.html
pieces.title: Five voices, coupled · the Kuramoto mirror as a test
pieces.caption:
**Amplified, or overridden?** Five sine voices from 216 to 226 Hz: one alone, five apart, coupled to the lock, let go, then coupled far too hard, evenly and with E as an anchor. The palace's own picture is built first (too little and nothing cooperates, too much and one voice dominates) and then measured.

dθᵢ/dt = 2π·fᵢ + (K/N)·K_receive,ᵢ·Σⱼ K_send,ⱼ·sin(θⱼ − θᵢ)

(how fast each voice turns) = (its own pitch) + (a pull toward every other voice, scaled by how much it listens and how hard each pulls)
pieces.near: The conatus of each oscillator is its natural frequency

verdicts.file: Spinoza Conatus — rich — five voices coupled.html
verdicts.why: Numbers all recomputed (lock 7.8495 Hz, 220.40 Hz, leads −16.8 … +21.5°, 6.74 dB = 6.99 + 20·log10(0.971), 6.7 dB at the output through the limiter), but the stated rule tests Kuramoto Coupling's line, not this section's: add a rule before the run for “amplified, not overridden”, saying “overridden” follows from “locked” and each voice's amplitude is fixed, so only the sum can be amplified; name the dominance test as the Kuramoto page's. Cut the caption's last two sentences, which give the answer before the walk.
